Can you feel the AGI, son? pic.twitter.com/SFuP3a8jqG — Chetaslua (@chetaslua) November 24, 2026 We are seeing a bunch of new outputs being circulated on X, and testers believe they're from Claude Opus 5.6. Of course, Anthropic hasn't announced anything, and not everyone is labeling this as Opus 5.6, but the results look like a step up from Opus 5.5. a 2D stick figure martial arts animation Made by Opus-next pic.twitter.com/CppBoNLEq3 In mid-October, some Opus 5.5 requests appeared to be landing on an unannounced model , which could have been an early Opus 5.6 or Fable 5.5 . Fable 5.5 never formally launched. Anthropic instead released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on November 9 . That said, things are heating up again. X user Leo said it's likely being tested with a subset of Claude users, some in Claude Code, some in Chat, and some not at all, and called it "quite a jump over Opus 5.5." Opus-next vs Fable 5.2 vs Fable 5.5 an SVG of pandas in a rainy bamboo forest pic.twitter.com/EsMedi5zXI Claude Opus 5.6 is likely now being tested for a subset of Claude users (some in Claude Code, some in Chat, and some without it anywhere), in a similar fashion to how Opus 5.5 was tested It's quite a jump over Opus 5.5 (comparison and prompt to check in replies) pic.twitter.com/GiAoHFqrEj Meanwhile, tipster Chetaslua posted that their run was routed from "Opus 5.5 Extra" and shared a Claude Code screenshot as proof, along with the code and prompt on GitHub . The Last Page is a hand-drawn-style short about a small fox, which they first shared as something "Opus 5.6 made... in pure code." There's no denying that the output looks incredible. Anime by Opus 5.6. Pure code, no external assets used. Music, song, visuals: everything is code. Now tell me this isn't an absolute masterpiece. pic.twitter.com/yRz6uicLuc They later posted a Jujutsu Kaisen fan film crediting Gege Akutami's characters, and called it an "absolute masterpiece," with the music, song, and visuals all made of code. It opens calmly, then breaks into a ruined-city battle. You have to see this for yourself to believe it. My personal favorites are Marcel's side-by-side comparison and Chetaslua's Three.js scene. Marc ran the same Last Page prompt on both models. The Opus 5.6 version tells the fox story clearly, while the Opus 5.5 version breaks down into glitchy shapes. Marc called the gap "insane." Opus 5.6 vs Opus 5.5 [animated SVG short film] both models on the exact same prompt and everything you see was made with pure code, no video generation involved. the gap is insane. look at how smoothly 5.6 handles the animation and looping. it’s already looking like the new… https://t.co/XzGOsD93bc pic.twitter.com/TesWooauZz The Three.js clip, which Chetaslua called "peak @threejs, no assets," shows a character sipping tea on a giant pelican as a seaside town floats up into the sky with the scene style changing. Opus 5.6 is peak @threejs , no assets. Can you feel the AGI, son? pic.twitter.com/SFuP3a8jqG Another user named Legit labeled it "Opus-next" and compared the result with Fable 5.2 and allegedly Fable 5.5 as well. All three are SVGs of a rainy bamboo forest. We can't verify they actually had Fable 5.5 or Opus 5.6, for that matter, so treat that label as one tester's claim. These are early, cherry-picked outputs, with no official confirmation that it is Opus 5.6. OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on November 17, and Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon a day later . If you're on Opus 5.5 Extra, you might already be trying it.
